records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb uses non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE; if process dies between them the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed URL — should use SET NX EX
records.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieved_recently?` implements throttling with two separate Redis commands: `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This is non-atomic; if the process dies after `SETNX` succeeds but before `EXPIRE` runs, the key can remain without a TTL, causing the method to treat the URL as "retrieved recently" indefinitely (permanent throttling for that `embed_url`). Using an atomic `SET` with `NX` + `EX` would avoid this.
records.stripped_text: topic_retriever.rb uses non-atomic SETNX/EXPIRE; if process dies between them the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently throttling that embed URL — should use SET NX EX

records.issue_text: Embed controller referer check is trivially forgeable via Referer header and only compares host; also silently 403s all embeds if site is renamed

The Referer header is client-supplied and can be forged by non-browser clients, so this is a weak/trust-on-header security check. The strict host equality (`!= SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) also means embeds will be denied whenever the embedding site’s host differs from the configured value (e.g., after a domain change) until settings are updated, matching the finding’s “renamed host breaks embeds”

This is a backwards-incompatible change that can break existing scripts/CI invoking `-c`, even if the underlying import path was refactored to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.
records.stripped_text: Disqus thor regression: --category option removed so posts lose their category
